properties.name: A finding is written the moment it is made and needs nobody's permission, and a session that reads the design at length and writes nothing is seen by the loop
properties.statement: Anthony, 2026-09-18, promoting flo2's F0 (2026-09-18) and this session's own lapse the same day. The distinction: intent (a requirement, a decision, a status) waits for the owner's word; a finding (a contradiction noticed, a measurement, a cause established) is the agent's own observation and is written before the answer, no permission owed. Two legs were missing and both are required: the INSTRUCTION — the capture skills say it, and a design rule carrying it is delivered on capture-intent, where-am-i, brainstorm, root-cause and triage-feedback; the DETECTOR — every loop signal counts nodes that exist, so loop_status must count THIS SESSION's reads and writes and say, in `next`, when a session that could write has read past a threshold and written nothing; the stop hook nudges once on the same inverse. Never for a read-only surface, and never as a question mid-thought (req:detecting-is-not-asking). The accepted req:session-memory-in-graph asked for this in July; its capability was still planned.
